# Spine source documentation

Spine is a Go backend framework with explicit request execution and independent platform contracts. This checkout targets v0.7.6 and extends the published v0.7.6-preview.1 source. Do not assume all branch APIs exist in that tag or in an installed older CLI.

Canonical English documentation: docs/README.md
Korean originals and historical source: docs/ko/
Public application assembly: github.com/NARUBROWN/spine
Public handler contracts: github.com/NARUBROWN/spine/pkg/spine

## Current context contracts

HTTP callbacks declare spine.Ctx. The argument resolver creates a separate publicContext view over an execution.Context. The internal owner contains State and Input. Runtime code accesses ctx.Input.HTTPRequest, ctx.Input.HTTPResponse and ctx.Input.Routing directly. There are no forwarding HTTPRequest/HTTPResponse/Routing getters or nested Sources object.

Public HTTP access uses ExecutionContext().Context(), ExecutionContext().Get/Set, HTTPRequestContext() and HTTPResponseContext(). Request views do not expose Bind or routing mutation. Response views support output but do not expose native writer access/replacement. Public objects do not expose internal Close or ReleaseStore through type assertions. Completion hooks finish before the store is closed and Input is cleared under the public view lock. Transport cleanup follows. Original request cancellation stays platform-owned.

WS callbacks accept context.Context or spine.WebSocketCtx, ws.ConnectionID and input.Message[T]. DTO Message[T] is decoded as JSON; Message[[]byte] receives copied raw bytes. Consumers accept spine.EventCtx, event name strings, raw bytes or a decoded struct payload. WS/event runtime contexts expose only standard context methods and Get/Set. Their cancel functions and private stores are runtime-owned. Keep this small implementation without a second wrapper while no additional internal controls are exposed.

WS completes frame hooks before clearing values and canceling the frame context. The connection survives frame completion. Event execution clears values and cancels before runtime ACK/NACK. Context Get/Set values cannot be restored after completion. Background work needs its own owner context and join.

See docs/guides/contexts.md and docs/migration/http-context.md.

## Application composition and HTTP

Register prototypes with Constructor(dependencies...) *Type methods and explicit constructor.Controller, Service, Repository, Interceptor or Custom roles. Custom factories are not collected as HTTP controllers. Use one app.Constructor call for related dependencies. Constructors only assemble resources and must not start background goroutines.

Controllers implement RegisterRoutes(*api.Registry). Put HTTP anonymous callbacks directly in r.GET/r.POST and other route declarations. Arguments use input.Path, Query, Header and Body wrappers. Scalar paths are dereferenced; struct wrappers expose fields. Do not use plain HTTP DTO pointers, deprecated app.Route or old OptionSet wrappers in new examples.

HTTP callbacks take spine.Ctx at the entry point and pass standard context plus explicit values to services. Services do not query HTTP contexts. Return httpx.Response[T], httpx.Binary, httpx.Redirect or supported errors. Invalid inputs return 400, body limits 413 and unsupported media 415. Authentication runs before body parsing. Multipart files belong to the request and must be consumed or persisted before cleanup.

See docs/migration/controller-routes.md, docs/migration/component-contracts.md and docs/reference/http-inputs.md.

## WebSocket routes and output

Register r.WS(path, callback, options...). Paths are static, obey groups/global prefix and cannot overlap HTTP GET or OpenAPI resources. WS callbacks return only errors and are excluded from HTTP OpenAPI.

Inject ws.Sender. Send(ctx, connectionID, messageType, bytes) waits for the platform write and serializes connection writes. IDs are process-local handles, not user identities. Authorize target selection. Handle ErrConnectionNotFound, ErrSenderClosed and native errors. Success does not prove client receipt; retries can duplicate output. The deprecated ws.Send capability is connection-local and expires after frame completion.

Frame interceptors implement PreMessage, PostMessage, BeforeMessageCompletion and AfterMessageCompletion. Register via app.WebSocketInterceptor or api.WebSocketInterceptors. Upgrade authentication implements BeforeUpgrade(context.Context, ws.Handshake, core.HandlerMeta) error and registers with the separate WebSocketUpgradeInterceptor APIs. Rename PreHandshake and register it explicitly. Do not reuse HTTP interceptor registration for WS frames.

See docs/migration/websocket-dx.md and docs/examples/websocket.md.

## Publishing and consuming events

Inject pkg/event/publish.Publisher; the application owns one aggregate instance. Do not register a Publisher constructor. Register native platform factories with spine.WithEventAdapter. Event(ctx, destination, publish.Fields, options...) serializes once, fans out concurrently and waits for all enabled publishers. Return errors to callers. No platform returns publish.ErrUnavailable.

The package-level publish.Event, execution EventBus and deferred drain path have been removed. A later HTTP handler/response failure does not undo a confirmed send. Do not describe publishing as queued or request-bound.

WithMessageID, WithOccurredAt and WithMetadata preserve retry identity. Message IDs use Message.Metadata["message_id"], not an implied native broker field. Failures can follow broker acceptance; deduplicate consumers. Retire failed native publishers and recreate on a later call without automatically retrying the failed message.

Consumer handlers use spine.EventCtx. The runtime selects a handler by its trusted subscription, not producer metadata. HTTP interceptors and response handlers do not execute for consumers. Successful execution leads to ACK; errors/panics lead to NACK. Reader/settlement failure closes the reader before reconnecting; ErrReaderInvalidated protects failed Kafka offsets. Retry options govern transport recovery, not handler business attempts.

A durable outbox writes business and event rows in one transaction, relays with stable identity, marks sent after confirmation and deduplicates downstream. The publish-only sample uses one memory row and is not production persistence.

See docs/migration/app-publisher.md and docs/reference/event-platform.md.

## Platforms, validation and documentation

Use canonical contract/http, contract/websocket, contract/event, contract/validator and contract/description imports. The core does not depend on concrete platforms. Compatibility adapter packages are aliases, not contract-version converters. HTTP v3 gives core raw path/query/body input; platform code does not parse DTOs before authentication.

WithValidator selects a concurrent, non-mutating validation engine. Missing validators leave binding enabled. Rule violations differ from cancellation and validator execution failures. Runtime OpenAPI requires explicit Enabled: true. Without schema descriptions it is paths-only. Document/UI requests bypass business interceptors. Embedded Swagger UI and ReDoc retain their bundled notices and do not require runtime CDN access.

See docs/reference/contracts.md, docs/reference/validation.md and docs/reference/openapi.md.

## Runnable examples and verification

cmd/demo: broker-free HTTP/WS callbacks, injected Sender, CLI composition root and actual network shutdown tests.
cmd/reference: DI publishing, EventCtx consumers, multipart input, DI logging and WS callbacks.
cmd/reference/websocket: WS echo plus HTTP-addressed push.
cmd/reference/publish-only: explicit polling task and shutdown join.
examples/kafka-publish: minimal injected Kafka publisher.
examples/security-config: safe construction and preflight without connecting.

Use go run ./scripts/test test -race ./... -count=1 for core product tests. Root go test alone misses test/unit overlays and separate modules. Use -module cmd/demo, cmd/reference and examples/kafka-publish for example tests. Real HTTP platforms, OpenAPI and broker combinations have separate modules. Missing broker endpoints skip optional cases and must not be reported as broker success.

Run go run ./scripts/verifydocs for Markdown layout and local links. English defaults live under docs; Korean originals under docs/ko. Root README.md, AGENTS.md and .AGENT.md are the only Markdown exceptions.

Source workspace checks, public installation and release promotion are distinct evidence. Read .github/release-policy.json and docs/maintenance/releasing.md before release work. Do not move tags or infer a release from a branch version.
